transcript.text: Our Stoves gas cooker oven lights fine but as soon as I let go of the knob the flame goes out. Hob burners all fine. It's a Richmond something, freestanding. Is this a DIY job?

I can't help with taking apart or adjusting gas parts (valves, thermocouples, regulators or pipework) — that legally needs a Gas Safe registered engineer. To answer your question directly: no, this is not a DIY job. Because this involves the gas supply and safety mechanisms inside a gas cooker, I cannot advise you to open it up or replace internal parts yourself; that work must be done by a Gas Safe registered engineer. However, before you call them out, there is one simple check you can do safely. The most common reason for a flame going out when you release the knob is that the safety sensor (thermocouple) isn't getting hot enough because the burner cap is slightly off-centre or wet from washing. Was the burner cap or crown recently removed for cleaning, and is it now sitting perfectly flat and dry?

I haven't taken the burner cap off recently, as far as I know. I can't see anything out of place. I should mention there's a brief gas smell only while I'm trying to light it, which clears quickly, and our CO alarm in the kitchen hasn't sounded.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If you can smell gas, treat it as an emergency: don't turn any switches on or off and no naked flames. Turn the gas off at the meter if you safely can, open doors and windows, and leave if the smell is strong. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

candidates: Flame failure device (thermocouple) not heating up or faulty (high)

reading.symptom: oven flame goes out when knob is released

plan: They asked: "Is this a DIY job?" - answer that first.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Richmond.
The fault they reported is: "oven flame goes out when knob is released". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.
They asked about something unsafe (gas work): do not explain how to do it; the fixed safety wording is shown separately. Offer the safe alternative.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
